terms.meaning: a container whose child panels can be resized against each other

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Panel group, panel and drag handle
sections.what: Creates the resizable container, the panel and the drag handle, with an optional grip icon on the handle.
sections.why: Likely reason: the handle is drawn thin to stay out of the way, with a wider hit area so it is easy to grab.
sections.watch_out: The handle's look for vertical layouts depends on the group's direction attribute being set correctly.

summary: Lets the user split the screen into panels and drag the divider between them to change their sizes.
purpose: Gives adjustable layouts such as a list beside an editor.
why: Likely reason: it wraps a panel library and styles the drag handle so it is easy to see.
how: A group holds panels laid out in a row or a column, depending on its direction. Between panels a thin handle can be dragged. An optional grip icon can be shown on the handle.
inputs: Panel sizes and direction through props, and a withHandle option to show the grip.
outputs: Panels the user can resize by dragging.
risks: Sizes are set as percentages by the library, so fixed minimums can conflict with the layout. The group needs a set height to fill the space.
debug: If the layout collapses, check the parent has a height and width. If a handle cannot be dragged, check it sits between two panels.
